judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Flat, functional checkpoint line followed by a stock threat ('blast you to oblivion') and a terse closing; the missing comma after 'Be gone' and the plain bureaucratic tone read as Westwood.

items.label: B
items.critique: Earnest, slightly stiff welcome ('fairest of all villages in the land of Nox', 'open warm arms of aid') with a cheery 'young Adventurer!' sign-off; exactly the campaign's formal-courteous town guard.

items.label: C
items.critique: Each line is built for flavour ('crack under our hammers', 'the slag road') rather than to tell the player anything; the coined local colour and rallying tone feel written to sound gritty.

items.label: D
items.critique: A jailer's plain, slightly dry warnings with an escalating 'Last warning'; short, practical, with Westwood's mild humour about the cells.

items.label: E
items.critique: Bare-bones informational line, then generic gratitude with an exclamation mark and 'Adventurer'; the repetition of 'deed(s)' is the kind of unpolished plainness Westwood has.

items.label: F
items.critique: Clipped, characterful slang ('Off the planks, bog rat!', 'Gate's open. Go on.') and an ellipsis page break used for drama; too stylised and voicey for Nox's plain guards.

items.label: G
items.critique: Pure directions: where to go, why (the shipment), which way to walk, repeated with a small variant; that redundant, navigational plainness is very Westwood.

items.label: H
items.critique: Too long and too many exclamation marks; stacked rhetorical beats ('his seal on this order says so', 'Will you go quietly, stranger?', '!?') read like a modern writer performing a gruff guard.

items.label: I
items.critique: Short and plain enough to pass, but the helmet aside and 'Go on, then.' feel like a deliberate attempt at terse Nox flavour; the three lines don't add up to a task the way Westwood's do.

items.label: J
items.critique: Concrete direction (ladder behind the clerk's desk) then a battle line and a homely joke about the Ogres' drums; the light, slightly silly closing is Westwood's humour.

tells: Westwood's guards mostly deliver information: who lives here, where to go, which path to take, often repeating the direction with small variation; the new texts spend their lines on mood and character instead.
Coined local slang and insults ('bog rat', 'off the planks', 'slag road') and gritty regional colour mark the new texts; Westwood uses generic terms and stock threats.
The new texts over-use exclamation marks, interrobangs and stacked short sentences in one speech; Westwood's lines are fewer and simpler, often a single sentence.
Westwood's tone is earnest or mildly comic and occasionally stiff/formal ('fairest of all villages'); the new texts aim for terse hard-boiled attitude.
Ellipsis page breaks used for dramatic pause, and rhetorical questions to the player, point to the new writer.
